PMC319880.scope: The control of araC transcription from the Pc promoter in Escherichia coli: the DNA sites in the ara regulatory region, which proteins occupy them (araC protein, CAP with cyclic AMP, RNA polymerase), and what that occupancy does to Pc activity. Induction of the araBAD operon from PBAD belongs to a sibling pathway and is OFF-PATHWAY here. The DNase protection and dimethyl sulfate methylation assays themselves, and any measurement that concerns araBAD expression only, are also off-pathway or excluded.

source.citation: Lee NL, Gielow WO, Wallace RG. Mechanism of araC autoregulation and the domains of two overlapping promoters, Pc and PBAD, in the L-arabinose regulatory region of Escherichia coli. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 1981 Feb;78(2):752-756.

PMC319880.audit: Every quote in this file is verbatim from C:/t/eval-fulltext/PMC319880.r3.txt and from nothing else; r3 is the authoritative text and both earlier revisions were discarded as evidence. Sections read in full: header, abstract, introduction, Materials and Methods, Results (DNA-Protein Contact Sites in the ara Regulatory Region; Polymerase binding sites at PBAD and Pc; The A Site Is a 'Classical' Operator for the araC Gene; The A Site Is Not Within PBAD), Discussion including the four numbered objections to Ogden et al., the abbreviations footnote, the legends of Figs. 1-7, acknowledgements and the reference list (read only to see what is cited). In r3 the body text runs continuously; only a few words remain displaced where lines cross the figure regions of page 3 (for instance the clause reporting that at 250 microM cAMP the CAP protected an additional region at -130 to -140 against DNase digestion, and the 'in the presence of polymerase' lead-in to the same paragraph). Those spans are readable but not quotable word for word, so they are skipped and the affected rows (I9, I10) carry other sentences instead. This is a transcription-control paper: it contains no metabolite conversion, so the content is protein-DNA occupancy (interactions) plus two gene-expression statements. Enzymes with a stated catalytic role: RNA polymerase holoenzyme (purified from E. coli NL20-000; attaches to Pc and protects a 65-bp region from -105 to -170, initiating araC transcription at -148; separately protects -39 to at least +24 at PBAD) - the only catalyst of an on-pathway transformation (R1). Named without a reaction of their own: DNase I and dimethyl sulfate (footprinting and methylation-protection reagents, excluded by SCOPE), the araC protein in its P1, P2 and P1' forms and the cyclic AMP-binding protein CAP (sequence-specific DNA-binding regulators, not catalysts here), and the unnamed 'enzymes required for the metabolism of L-arabinose' encoded by araBAD (a class, off-pathway). No transport step and no compartment appears anywhere in the paper, so the PathBank hint's 'Cytosol' was not carried over. Record-level observations about the hint, not about the paper: PathBank models CAP in pathway 703792 as nucleic_acids id 275, nucleotide_type DNA, although CAP is a protein and PathBank holds the correct protein record (proteins id 10248, cAMP-activated global transcriptional regulator CRP, UniProt P0ACJ8); 'Ara inducer gene' is nucleic_acids id 925, gene_name AraI, DNA; and the pathway uses Activation on six edges against Inhibition on one, so its signs are deliberate claims.

interactions.note: Full sentence restored from r3. The A site lies within the RNA polymerase binding site at Pc and is the operator locus for araC autoregulation. The A site has a greater affinity for P2 than for P1 (complete protection at protein/DNA = 2 for P2 against 20 for P1); the B-site half of the following sentence is off-pathway (I15). The paper identifies its A and B sites with Ogden et al.'s araO and araI by location. PathBank PW_I016130 labels this edge activation; the paper states occupancy.
